title: Finalize PRD for Console “Optimization suggestions” beta (batching + caching only) and align scope with Optimize
text:
Finalize PRD for Console “Optimization suggestions” beta (batching + caching only) and align scope with Optimize

## Summary
We are shipping a beta “Optimization suggestions” experience in Redwood Console that surfaces cost-reduction opportunities with clear latency/reliability tradeoffs. This ticket exists to (1) author/finalize the PRD, and (2) align Console + Optimize scope/ownership so design + engineering can execute without churn.

This beta scope is explicitly limited to batching and caching suggestions. Quantization and other Optimize modules can be referenced but must not be launched in this view.

## Problem statement
Customers want to reduce inference spend, but the knobs (batching, caching, routing, etc.) are hard to reason about safely in production. Today, Redwood provides primitives and dashboards, but not an actionable “what should I do next?” workflow. Early customer conversations indicate strong interest, but also low trust if estimates feel inflated or risk is unclear.

## Goals (beta)
1) Make cost optimization actionable
- Surface the top opportunities by route/model (and project) with estimated savings.
- Provide a “why” and a “how to enable” path (deep links to config pages).

2) Improve user trust
- Show assumptions and inputs used to compute estimates.
- Show confidence and conservative risk labels.
- Avoid language that implies guarantees or contractual commitments.

3) Create a closed loop
- Instrument: impression → expand → dismiss → apply-click (and config-save where possible).
- Use telemetry to learn which suggestions are useful and where UX is confusing.

## Non-goals (beta)
- No quantization recommendation UI within the Suggestions view.
- No automatic application of suggestions without explicit user confirmation.
- No customer-specific savings commitments.
- No attempt to “prove” savings to the penny; we are shipping estimates with caveats.

## Primary users / personas
- Platform / infra engineer: owns shared inference routes and cares about SLOs.
- ML engineer: owns model choice and serving configuration, cares about quality and latency.
- FinOps / Eng manager (secondary): reviews cost deltas, needs simple risk communication.

## User stories
1) As a platform engineer, I can see the biggest cost-saving opportunities for a specific route/model pair, with a clear explanation of likely latency impact and a conservative risk label.
2) As an ML engineer, I can drill into a suggestion and understand: the rationale, assumptions, estimated savings, and exactly what setting to change.
3) As a team lead, I can share a suggestion detail view and have stakeholders understand what “risk” means (performance/reliability, not security).
4) As an admin, I can control access via RBAC and selectively enable beta via feature flags.

## Scope definition (must-haves)
### Console UX (Suggestions view)
- Entry point: Optimize → Suggestions (behind feature flag).
- List/table view with:
  - Route, model, suggestion type (batching/caching)
  - Estimated savings: $/day and % (with time window)
  - Estimated performance impact: p50/p95 latency delta (direction + magnitude)
  - Risk level: Low / Medium / High with tooltip and explanation
  - Confidence indicator (v0) and staleness (stale_as_of)
- Details drawer with:
  - “Why we recommend this” narrative (human-readable)
  - Assumptions / inputs used (e.g., QPS window, current cache hit rate)
  - Guardrails: when NOT to use / what to monitor
  - Deep links to config pages (batching and caching settings)
- Sorting/filtering (beta minimum):
  - Sort by savings (default), filter by route, model, suggestion type, risk level
- Empty states:
  - No suggestions (eligible but none)
  - Insufficient telemetry / compute lag
  - Feature not enabled / RBAC denied
- Copy + disclaimers:
  - “Estimated savings” language; never “you will save”
  - Risk explicitly defined as performance/reliability risk

### Backend/API
- Suggestions API with stable IDs and pagination (supports sorting/filtering).
- RBAC: read-only permission for viewing suggestions.
- Include fields needed for UX: savings estimates, latency deltas, risk label + rationale, confidence, stale_as_of.

### Estimation pipeline
- v0 savings estimator for batching/caching using aggregate telemetry.
- Conservative defaults if inputs are missing; reflect uncertainty.
- Cadence: periodic compute (hourly or daily; final choice in ADR).

### Observability + funnel
- Dashboard for API health (latency/5xx) and compute lag.
- Funnel dashboard with breakdowns by org, model, route, region.

## Out of scope (explicit)
- Writing configuration automatically.
- Suggesting model changes.
- Cross-org comparisons or any data that could hint at other tenants.
- Advanced “what-if simulator”.

## Success metrics (beta)
### Adoption / engagement
- % of eligible orgs who visit Suggestions within 14 days of enablement.
- Funnel: impression → expand rate, and expand → apply-click rate.

### Trust / quality signals
- Dismiss reasons captured (where implemented) and distribution.
- Support volume: number of tickets tagged “suggestions estimate inaccurate” per enabled org.
- UX research comprehension score: users can correctly explain savings + risk meaning.

### Reliability
- Suggestions API p95 latency within budget and <1% error rate during beta.
- Compute freshness: X% of suggestions updated within the advertised window.

## GA criteria (proposed; to confirm in PM-857)
- Stable API contract + stable IDs, no breaking schema changes for 30 days.
- Risk labels: internal review indicates low confusion; <N support tickets per M enabled orgs about “risk is unclear”.
- Estimate reasonableness: validation plan meets acceptance thresholds (see Applied ML validation doc).
- SRE sign-off on runbook + alerts.

## Rollout plan (beta)
- Feature flag gating per org.
- Dogfood: Redwood internal orgs + 1–2 friendly accounts.
- Private beta: 5–10 accounts meeting telemetry readiness criteria.
- Expand beta: 20–30 accounts; re-evaluate after 2 weeks.
- Rollback: disable feature flag; ensure UI handles “not enabled” state cleanly.

## Milestones (target)
- PRD + IA alignment complete: 2026-02-07
- Design spec final (table + drawer + copy): 2026-02-14
- API contract + stable IDs finalized (ADR complete): 2026-02-18
- Internal dogfood start: 2026-02-21
- Private beta start: 2026-03-03
- Beta expansion decision: 2026-03-17

## Open questions to resolve in this PRD
1) Confidence: do we ship as a badge (e.g., “High/Med/Low confidence”) or as an “inputs complete” indicator in beta?
2) Savings time window: last 7 days vs last 24h (and how to communicate volatility).
3) “Applied” definition: do we count apply-click only, or do we integrate with config-save events (phase 2)?
4) Risk mapping: ensure consistent definition across estimator + UX copy; confirm thresholds in ADR.
5) What is the minimum filtering needed for usability (route + model + risk), vs shipping in iteration 2?

## Ownership / RACI (beta)
- PRD owner: Aditya Rao (Optimize) + Marissa Cole (Console) (shared)
- Console UX spec: Tessa Morgan / Kenji Nakamura
- Backend API: Chloe Martin
- Telemetry taxonomy + dashboards: Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman
- Applied ML estimator + risk inputs: Dr. Maya Srinivasan / Jonas Weber / Sana Farid
- Rollout readiness: Sean Gallagher (SRE)
- Docs + in-product education: Elliot Price / Jean-Paul Laurent

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] PRD finalized and linked in ticket with explicit “in scope / out of scope” sections.
- [ ] Scope aligned across Console + Optimize leads: batching/caching only for beta; quantization explicitly excluded.
- [ ] Clear definitions:
  - [ ] Savings estimate presentation ($/day and %), including time window and caveats.
  - [ ] Risk definition (performance/reliability) and how it will be explained in UI copy.
  - [ ] Confidence / uncertainty surfaced in some form.
- [ ] Milestones and GA criteria draft included and agreed as input to PM-857.
- [ ] Instrumentation plan included: required events and properties.
- [ ] Links added to relevant design specs/ADRs and owning tickets (ENG/DES).

## Links / references
- Confluence PRD (draft): optimization-suggestions-console-ux-beta-prd.json
- IA + user flows: suggestions-view-information-architecture-and-user-flows.json
- Risk definitions + copy: risk-level-definition-and-copy-guidelines.json
- ADRs: suggestions API contract + stable IDs; risk scoring model v0
- Events taxonomy draft: suggestions-events-taxonomy.json

## Updates
- 2026-01-14 (Marissa): Created ticket after kickoff; need single source of truth for beta scope.
- 2026-02-03 (Aditya): Added explicit non-goals (no quantization UI, no auto-apply). Drafted success metrics + GA criteria proposal.
- 2026-02-11 (Marissa): Aligned with Design on table + drawer pattern; requested copy to avoid “guaranteed savings”.
- 2026-02-18 (Aditya): Synced with Applied ML on conservative estimator framing; added open question on confidence UX.
- 2026-02-26 (Marissa): Ready for final PRD pass + sign-off from Console Eng + SRE; pushing remaining decisions to PM-857 where appropriate.
